STEP 02 · INTERACTIVE PATIENT CHALLENGE

Four patients. Similar blood pressure. Different organ-damage patterns.

Choose any two fictional patients. Their blood pressures look similar — but their illustrative HyTwin profiles tell different stories.

Educational simulation only: these cases and HyperScores are invented, not calculated by the private HyTwin model. The clinical outcome descriptions are based on the published research and apply to study groups, not to these fictional individuals.
STEP 03 · MODEL PHENOTYPES

Six pathways. Different patterns of damage.

HyTwin identifies six organ-dominant phenotypes. These are patterns of observed measurements and outcomes — not six stages of severity.

Important nuance: the Lipoprotein group showed lower mortality relative to the other trajectories in the published study, but it had more nonfatal metabolic outcomes. The Liver trajectory had limited numbers and was less reproducible; it should be interpreted cautiously.
STEP 04 · YOUR RESEARCH · UK BIOBANK + ARIC

Does the pattern of damage differ by sex and ethnicity?

Explore reported associations from the working manuscript. These are population-level findings, not a prediction of what will happen to an individual.

Select a group

The available ethnicity groups differ between UK Biobank and ARIC. The manuscript also includes an “Other” category; this explorer focuses on groups with a reported sex-specific association.

The bigger picture: sex matters

Across ethnic groups in both datasets, males had higher HyperScores than females. Ethnicity-related differences in trajectory distribution were more apparent among females. In the UK Biobank, overall HyperScore differences between ethnic groups were not statistically significant (p = 0.056).

Caution: the UK Biobank ethnic subgroups were unevenly represented, particularly Chinese (n=78) and Black (n=196) participants. Odds ratios shown below compare membership in one trajectory with membership in all other trajectories; they are not absolute probabilities or direct ethnic-group risk ratios.
